angularDiameterSource: EHT Collaboration (2022, ApJL 930, L12; arXiv:2311.08680), Sgr A* Paper I, Table 1: angular shadow diameter d_sh = 48.7 +/- 7.0 microarcseconds, determined from EHT data alone.
distanceSource: GRAVITY Collaboration (2022, A&A 657, L12; arXiv:2112.07478), Table 1, four-star fit: R0 = 8277 +/- 9 pc. The stellar orbits in this system are angular sizes converted at this distance, as that fit does.
radiusSource: Radius: half the angular shadow diameter 48.7 +/- 7.0 microarcseconds measured from EHT data alone (EHT Collaboration 2022, ApJL 930, L12, Sgr A* Paper I, Table 1), at the distance 8277 pc of GRAVITY Collaboration (2022, A&A 657, L12, Table 1): 24.35e-6 x 8277 au = 0.2015 au = 30,150,695 km at 149,597,870.7 km per au. It is the size of the dark region an observer sees, not an event horizon. GM from the mass 4.297 +/- 0.012 million solar masses (GRAVITY 2022, Table 1) times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2.

shape.qualification: A black sphere at the measured shadow radius: the dark region an observer sees, not an event horizon or a surface.

massSource: GRAVITY Collaboration (2022, A&A 657, L12; arXiv:2112.07478), Table 1, four-star fit: M = 4.297 +/- 0.012 million solar masses at R0 = 8277 pc.
